title: A drought-fitted regional runoff threshold was zero in four annual models at 138 south-east Australian catchments
abstract: We tested whether a free output threshold adds information beyond a runoff gain. We used annual CAMELS-AUS v2.03 data at 138 mainland south-east Australian catchments. Reference rain models used 1951-1996. Regional corrections used 1997-2009, and testing used 2010-2021. The rule was gain times the positive part of reference runoff minus a threshold. With AGCD and SILO rain and linear and curved reference models, all four fitted thresholds were zero. Joint-rule predictions were thus identical to scale-only predictions. The main gain was 0.706 and test mean squared error was 0.09173, compared with 0.15407 unchanged and 0.09721 for a threshold-only rule. Full-refit spatial and year-block ranges did not clearly rank threshold-only and scale rules. Positive thresholds occurred in refitted samples. Boundary estimates prevent a regular confidence-interval interpretation. A common output threshold is not a physical storage threshold, and the tested family excludes positive affine offsets. This is a scoped null test on reused data, not evidence that physical thresholds are absent. Code, predictions, profile losses, all draws, source hashes and independent optimization checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Drought-fitted threshold and gain compared with scale-only prediction in 2010-2021. Error ranges include full refitting. Drought profile losses select zero added threshold in all four variants.
